Mapped_rxn: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

So reactants: an alkyne attached to Si (trimethylsilyl alkyne) and a methyl ester of a phenylpropanoic acid? Actually O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])... That's a methyl ester of a carbonyl attached to a phenyl chain. The product is a methyl ester with a cyclopropene? Wait product: [CH3][O][C](=O)[C]1(/[CH]=[CH]/[c]2... ) [CH]=[C]1[Si]... This matches our target: methyl ester with a cyclopropene (C= C) attached to Si? Actually our target has a cyclopropene (C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)). That's a cyclopropene with a SiMe3 substituent. The product in template has [CH]=[C]1[Si]... which is a cyclopropene? Yes, a three-membered ring with a double bond and SiMe3.

Thus this template exactly matches our target molecule. The template ID is not given directly; we have reaction_id and template_hash. It says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". In the result, we have "reaction_id". Possibly that is the template_id. Usually template catalog entries have "template_id". But here we have "reaction_id". Might be the identifier to use with other tools like get_template. The tool get_template expects template_id as string. So we should use reaction_id as template_id.
